definitions.definition: The ultimate — dharmatā, buddha-nature, the dharmakāya — is empty of everything other than itself (all adventitious conventional phenomena) but not empty of its own nature and qualities.

In Kongtrul's presentation, the Great Madhyamaka view of the final turning, suited to meditative experience; in Mipham's sense, the unconditioned wisdom's emptiness of the adventitious, which does not exclude its also being empty of own-nature.
Emptiness of own-nature; for the Jonang it is true of all conventional phenomena but not of the ultimate.
The Madhyamaka of Nāgārjuna's reasonings, in which every phenomenon including the ultimate is empty of own-nature; in Kongtrul's presentation valid especially for cutting elaborations.

cross_language.note: Sanskrit phrasing, not a Sanskrit school name

equivalents.note: the rangtong reading of niḥsvabhāvatā applied to all phenomena

definitions.definition: Dolpopa's name for the definitive Madhyamaka of the third turning, the Maitreya texts, Nāgārjuna's hymns and the Kālacakra, in which the ultimate is other-empty.
Kongtrul's name for the other-emptiness Madhyamaka presented as the summit of the sūtra tenets.

notes: The same name is used in the Nyingma (Rongzom, Mipham) for a Madhyamaka of the union of appearance and emptiness, not identical with Dolpopa's usage.

definitions.definition: The ultimate: buddha-nature, empty of other, permanent; the object of self-aware wisdom.

equivalents.note: standard translation equivalent

definitions.definition: Conventional phenomena, adventitious and empty of own-nature, which conceal the ultimate.

equivalents.note: standard translation equivalent

definitions.definition: The ultimate aspect of the basis of all: buddha-nature as primordial wisdom, distinguished from the conventional ālaya-consciousness.

cross_language.note: reconstructed Sanskrit; not a common Indian term

definitions.definition: The obscurations that are other than the ultimate, separable from it and never of its nature.

equivalents.note: the adventitious defilements of the tathāgatagarbha literature

term: rnam kun mchog ldan gyi stong nyid
literal: emptiness endowed with all supreme aspects

definitions.definition: The Kālacakra's name for the ultimate as empty form joined with unchanging bliss, which Dolpopa equates with the other-empty dharmatā.
An emptiness that is a mere nothing; for the Jonang the error of taking the ultimate to be a non-affirming negation.

term: rtag brtan ther zug g.yung drung

definitions.definition: The fourfold description of the ultimate, taken from the tathāgatagarbha sūtras and Kālacakra, which the Jonang hold to be literally true of the dharmakāya.

cross_language.note: the sūtras' predicates of the dharmakāya

definitions.definition: Dolpopa's designation for his own restatement of the definitive teaching of the age of perfection.
The thoroughly established nature: self-illuminating wisdom free of subject-object duality, the ultimate.

equivalents.note: Tāranātha's self-aware wisdom is ultimate; Indian svasaṃvedana is a feature of cognition in the pramāṇa tradition

definitions.definition: The Kālacakra six-branch vajra-yoga — withdrawal, meditative stability, vitality-control, retention, recollection, samādhi — the principal Jonang practice.

equivalents.note: Tibetan translation of the Kālacakra term

definitions.definition: The completion-stage practice of the Kālacakra, the six-branch yoga, by which empty form and unchanging bliss are realized.
Forms that appear in the practice of the six-branch yoga, not made of matter, the support for unchanging bliss; the signs of withdrawal are their first appearance.

term: mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen po

definitions.definition: The immutable bliss of the Kālacakra, joined with empty form; for Dolpopa an aspect of the other-empty ultimate.

Buddha-nature as the ultimate itself: permanent, empty of adventitious stains, not empty of the buddha-qualities, present in all beings (Tibetan de bzhin gshegs pa'i snying po / bde gshegs snying po).
Read by Kongtrul as the Great Madhyamaka's other-empty ground; by Mipham as the union of luminosity and emptiness.

cross_language.form: de bzhin gshegs pa'i snying po; bde gshegs snying po

definitions.definition: The ultimate itself, permanent and the true self (perfection of self), not newly produced at awakening.
Definitive meaning: for Dolpopa, the teaching that the ultimate is other-empty, found in the third turning and the Kālacakra.
Provisional meaning: for Dolpopa, middle-wheel statements that the ultimate too is self-empty; for Butön, conversely, the literal tathāgatagarbha teaching.
The thoroughly established nature: the ultimate, self-aware wisdom, empty of the imputational and other-powered natures (other-empty).
The other-powered nature, dualistic consciousness: conventional and self-empty in Tāranātha's reading.
The conventional basis of all, the ground of saṃsāric imprints, to be distinguished from the ultimate ālaya-wisdom.

The tantra, the deity and the primordial buddha whose teaching of the age of perfection and six-branch yoga is the heart of the Jonang; its 'emptiness endowed with all supreme aspects' names the other-empty ultimate.
In the Jonang, the Kālacakra six-branch vajra-yoga, the main practice for realizing the other-empty ultimate (restricted practice).
For Dolpopa, the age of perfection whose definitive teaching — the other-empty ultimate — he claims to restore.
The practice of cutting ego-clinging, the root of the four māras, by applying the view of the Perfection of Wisdom, especially through the visualized gift of the body in frightening places.

literal: the object to be cut; the 'domain' of cutting

definitions.definition: Both the name of the practice and what it targets: the root of mind, self-clinging.
In Chöd: the obstructive, the unobstructive, the māra of elation and the māra of conceit, all rooted in the last.

equivalents.note: Chöd's four māras are a different set from the classical four (aggregates, afflictions, death, divine son) though the same word is used

definitions.definition: External objects of the senses that provoke attachment and aversion and so obstruct.
The thoughts and emotions that arise in the mind without any tangible object.
Attachment and pride in one's attainments, signs, reputation and good fortune.
Self-fixation, the root of the other three; cutting it cuts all four.
The grasping at a self that is the real demon and the root of the four māras; what Chöd cuts.
The ignorance that grasps a self, root of the three poisons and so of all disease.
The spirits, helpful and harmful, that Chöd teaches to be the display of one's own mind.
Spirit influences that obstruct; in Chöd they are guests to be fed and karmic creditors to be repaid.
One of the conditions of disease and one branch of medicine; spirit diseases require ritual as well as treatment.

equivalents.note: Āyurvedic 'seizers' (bhūtavidyā) and Tibetan gdon share the medical category

definitions.definition: Charnel grounds, lonely springs, trees and passes where spirits dwell, sought out by Chöd practitioners because fear arises there.
The visualized offering of one's own body, transformed into nectar, to the four guests (restricted practice: summary only).
The recipients of the body-offering: the Three Jewels, the protectors, the six classes of beings, and harmful spirits and karmic creditors.
The offering of the body visualized as white nectar, pleasing and pacifying the guests.
The offering of the body as flesh and blood to the demonic guests (visualized; restricted summary).
The wrathful black form of Vajrayoginī as which the practitioner's consciousness arises in Chöd.
Prajñāpāramitā personified as the mother of all buddhas; Machig is her emanation.

equivalents.note: the perfection of wisdom as teaching and as the personified mother

definitions.definition: A trumpet of human thighbone blown in Chöd to summon the guests and cut through fear.

term: ḍamaru (Tibetan da ma ru; gcod rnga)

definitions.definition: The large double-headed drum of Chöd, played with the bell while singing the liturgy.

cross_language.form: da ma ru; gcod rnga (Chöd drum)

definitions.definition: The renunciant with no possessions who gathers merit by offering his own body — the 'kusāli's accumulation' of the preliminaries.
The (often wandering) practitioner of Chöd, known for practice in haunted places and for being called on in epidemics and at deaths.
In Chöd, the transference of consciousness into the sky as the wrathful ḍākinī at the start of the body-offering.
The charnel ground (dur khrod), prime place for Chöd practice.
The view of Chöd, applied as practice to cut clinging; personified as the Great Mother.
The teaching whose mantra 'pacifies all suffering', from which Pacification takes its name.

cross_language.form: shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa

definitions.definition: 'Mahāmudrā Chöd': Machig's Chöd understood as resting in the mind's nature once clinging is cut.
The tradition and practice of pacifying suffering through the realization of the Perfection of Wisdom, named after the Heart Sūtra's mantra that 'pacifies all suffering'.
The science of medicine, one of the five major sciences, taught in the Four Tantras.

equivalents.note: overlapping medical science; Sowa Rigpa adds Buddhist causation and other sources

definitions.definition: The three principles rlung, mkhris pa and bad kan that sustain the body in balance and cause disease when disturbed; they arise from desire, hatred and delusion.

equivalents.note: same technical term; the Tibetan system derives the three from the three poisons

definitions.definition: The light, rough, cool, subtle, hard and mobile nyepa, arising from desire; seated chiefly in the lower body; the mount of the mind and mover of the others.

equivalents.note: corresponding doṣa; Tibetan qualities and causal derivation differ in detail

definitions.definition: The hot, sharp, oily nyepa, arising from hatred; seated chiefly in the middle of the body; digestion, heat and complexion.

equivalents.note: corresponding doṣa; Tibetan qualities and causal derivation differ in detail

definitions.definition: The heavy, cool, oily, stable nyepa, arising from delusion; seated chiefly in the upper body; firmness, moisture and joints.

equivalents.note: corresponding doṣa; Tibetan qualities and causal derivation differ in detail

definitions.definition: The seven constituents: nutritive essence, blood, flesh, fat, bone, marrow and regenerative fluid.

equivalents.note: the seven dhātus of Āyurveda

definitions.definition: The three excretions: faeces, urine and sweat.

equivalents.note: Āyurvedic malas

definitions.definition: Earth, water, fire, wind and space, of which body, nyepa, tastes and medicines are composed.

equivalents.note: the same five elements

definitions.definition: Sweet, sour, salty, bitter, hot and astringent, each from a pair of elements.

equivalents.note: rasa in its pharmacological sense

definitions.definition: The eight potencies of medicines — heavy, oily, cool, blunt, light, rough, hot, sharp.

equivalents.note: Āyurveda counts two or eight vīryas

definitions.definition: The three tastes after digestion (sweet, sour, bitter) that determine a food's or medicine's later effect.

equivalents.note: Āyurvedic post-digestive effect

definitions.definition: The channels of the body (four kinds) and the pulse read at the wrist.

equivalents.note: channel/vessel in the medical sense

definitions.definition: Reading the radial pulse with three fingers on both wrists; the chief tactile diagnosis.

equivalents.note: Āyurvedic pulse examination is a later development; the Tibetan system is independent in detail

definitions.definition: Examination of urine while warm, cooling and cold, for colour, vapour, odour, bubbles, sediment and film.
The teacher of the Four Tantras, sitting in Tanaduk and emanating Rigpé Yeshe and Yilé Kyé; object of the physician's devotion.
The city of medicine in which the Four Tantras were taught, surrounded by mountains of medicines.

cross_language.note: Sanskrit equivalent as usually given; moderate confidence

definitions.definition: A traditional practitioner of Sowa Rigpa, especially in Ladakh, the Himalaya and Mongolia.

notes: Etymology (Mongolian emchi) recalled with moderate confidence; not asserted.

definitions.definition: Rejuvenation regimens and essences that restore vigour and prolong life (in their retreat forms, which restrict ordinary food, restricted: summary only).

equivalents.note: the rejuvenation branch

definitions.definition: The branch concerned with virility and fertility.

equivalents.note: the same branch of the eight

definitions.definition: Mercury detoxified and processed into an ash used as an ingredient of the precious pills. Restricted: the tradition holds that improperly processed mercury is a poison and that the process belongs only to qualified masters; no procedure recorded.

equivalents.note: calcined metal preparations of Rasaśāstra

definitions.definition: Compound pills containing precious substances and processed metals, consecrated and taken under dietary rules (summary only).
The basic division of all disorders into hot (chiefly mkhris pa and blood) and cold (chiefly rlung and bad kan), treated by opposite means.
The not-understanding of selflessness that is the distant cause of all disease.

equivalents.note: standard translation equivalent

definitions.definition: Desire, hatred and delusion, arising from ignorance and producing rlung, mkhris pa and bad kan.
One of the fifteen subdivisions of the nyepa: seated in the crown; swallowing, breathing, clarity of mind and senses.

equivalents.note: corresponding Āyurvedic subtype; seats and functions differ in detail

notes: Seats and functions recalled with moderate confidence; correspondence to the Āyurvedic subtype is the usual one.

equivalents.note: corresponding Āyurvedic subtype; seats and functions differ in detail

notes: Seats and functions recalled with moderate confidence; correspondence to the Āyurvedic subtype is the usual one.

equivalents.note: corresponding Āyurvedic subtype; seats and functions differ in detail

equivalents.note: corresponding Āyurvedic subtype; seats and functions differ in detail

equivalents.note: corresponding Āyurvedic subtype; seats and functions differ in detail

equivalents.note: corresponding Āyurvedic subtype; seats and functions differ in detail

equivalents.note: corresponding Āyurvedic subtype; seats and functions differ in detail

equivalents.note: corresponding Āyurvedic subtype; seats and functions differ in detail

notes: Seats and functions recalled with moderate confidence; correspondence to the Āyurvedic subtype is the usual one.

definitions.definition: A 'rough' external therapy for hot and blood disorders (summary only; sites and methods not recorded).

equivalents.note: the same therapy

definitions.definition: Cauterizing or warming points with burning herbal cones, chiefly for cold and rlung disorders (summary only).
Massage with oils, especially for rlung disorders and in daily conduct.

equivalents.note: oil massage

definitions.definition: The eight branches of medicine in the Four Tantras: body, children, women, spirits, wounds, poisons, old age (rejuvenation) and virility.

equivalents.note: the Tibetan list has women's diseases where Āyurveda has the treatment of the head (śālākya)

definitions.definition: The non-sectarian attitude and programme: respecting, receiving and preserving every authentic lineage in its own terms.
Impartiality, paired with ris med in the formula phyogs med ris med.
Jamgön Kongtrul's five great collections: of Knowledge, of Kagyu Mantra, of Precious Treasures, of Instructions, and of Extensive Teachings.

term: sgrub brgyud shing rta chen po brgyad
literal: the eight great chariots of practice lineages

definitions.definition: The eight practice lineages into which Tibetan practice is organized: Nyingma, Kadam, Lamdre, Marpa Kagyu, Shangpa Kagyu, Shije and Chöd, Kālacakra six-branch yoga, Orgyen Nyendrub.
The seven transmissions held by Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo: the long oral lineage, earth treasures, rediscovered treasures, mind treasures, recollection, pure vision and the hearing lineage.

notes: Distinct from Tāranātha's 'seven instruction lineages' (bka' babs bdun ldan), a set of Indian siddha lineages.

definitions.definition: The thirteen Indian treatises at the core of the Rimé-influenced monastic curriculum, annotated by Khenpo Shenga.
